clue.text: Compassionate fellow wearing a colour

indicators.note: whatever is worn goes around the wearer, so one piece is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: a fellow is a man
a hue is a colour or shade

explanation.surface: A kindly man dressed in a particular colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' puts the colour around the fellow, as clothes go around the body that wears them.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane describes someone showing kindness, mercy and sympathy toward others, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Generous type has been exceptionally significant element

indicators.note: done in an exceptional, out-of-the-ordinary way, so the letters leave their usual order

blocks.note: taken as written
a factor is an element that contributes significantly to a result

explanation.surface: A generous person has proved an exceptionally important part of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptionally' reads as an intensifier of 'significant', but it works backwards on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactor is a person who gives money or help freely, so a generous sort of person.

clue.text: Detectives probing a boss who takes LSD?

definitions.note: short for 'one who takes LSD', a noun phrase

indicators.note: to probe is to poke inside something, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police
A plus HEAD, a head being a boss

explanation.surface: Police investigate a manager who uses drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police. The definition runs on from 'a boss', so those words do double duty in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid is slang for the drug LSD, and an acidhead is a habitual user of it.

clue.text: A group said to grow

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so we want the sound rather than the spelling

blocks.note: a crew is a group working together

explanation.surface: A band or team is said to be getting bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'a crew' out loud and it matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest or debts accrue when they build up and increase over time, a synonym for growing.

clue.text: A host with a bit of money as a neighbour

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase; the answer is an adjective meaning next door

blocks.note: taken as written
a disc jockey hosts a radio show or party
taken as written
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: A party host with a little cash living next door.
explanation.walkthrough: A host is a DJ here, the presenter of a show, not someone giving a dinner party.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adjacent lies right beside something else, just as a neighbour lives next to you.

clue.text: What you’ll see at funfairs – old clown getting crazy

blocks.note: Coco the Clown was a famous circus clown of the twentieth century
nuts is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A fairground scene with an elderly clown losing his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco was a celebrated clown with Bertram Mills Circus in Britain; the name is common crossword shorthand for any clown.
explanation.definitionFit: A coconut shy is a traditional fairground stall where players throw balls to knock coconuts off posts.

clue.text: Liking to combine power with charm

blocks.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
to enchant is to charm

explanation.surface: A fondness for mixing authority with personal charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' looks like a noun beside 'power', but it is the verb ENCHANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong fondness or taste for something, a synonym of the noun liking.

clue.text: Relation in Taunton

indicators.note: something within a word is contained by it, so look inside the letters that follow

blocks.note: the letters run inside this place name

explanation.surface: A family member living in a Somerset town.
explanation.walkthrough: Taunton is the county town of Somerset in England; the answer sits in its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Your parent's sister is a family member, one kind of relative by blood or marriage.

clue.text: King perched up for assignment

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
perched means sat on something

explanation.surface: A monarch sitting high up in order to carry out a duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' seems to go with 'perched', a king sitting on high, but it reverses the whole string.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work given to someone, which is what an assignment is.

clue.text: Beast sailor found by a lake

blocks.note: a jack or jack tar is an old word for a sailor
taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A wild animal discovered by a seaman beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a traditional nickname for a sailor, as in jack tar.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackal is a wild dog-like scavenger of Africa and Asia, so an example of an animal.

clue.text: We had rings provided for happy ceremonies?

blocks.note: we had contracts to we'd
a ding is a ringing sound, as of a bell

explanation.surface: A couple saying they had rings ready for their marriage celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pushes wedding rings, but the rings here are the sounds a bell makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding is a marriage service, normally a joyful celebration, so the plural fits joyous rites.

clue.text: Think about opposing pattern for further development

blocks.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a template is a pattern to copy from

explanation.surface: Weighing up an alternative design before developing it further.
explanation.walkthrough: The closing phrase only rounds out the surface, suggesting an idea being considered before it is developed.
explanation.definitionFit: To contemplate something is to consider it thoughtfully and at length, a synonym of thinking it over.

clue.text: Citation at the bottom of page 6

definitions.note: a cross-reference to 6-across, whose answer means liking

indicators.note: in a down entry, being at the bottom means coming after, so this part is placed second

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for page
a citation is a reference to a source

explanation.surface: A footnote reference printed at the foot of page six.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Page 6' looks like a page number, but the 6 is the definition, pointing to the answer at 6-across, PENCHANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A preference is a greater liking for one thing over another, so it matches a penchant or fondness.

clue.text: Organise country for charitable act

blocks.note: to do an event is to organise or put it on
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Mobilising a whole country to help a good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organise' looks like an anagram signal for 'country', but the letters do not fit; it gives DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift to a good cause, and giving it is an act of charity.

clue.text: intrepid female totally unable to listen?

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
with no ears at all, one could not listen

explanation.surface: A daring woman who is completely deaf.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical invented word: lacking ears entirely, so quite unable to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means bold and daring, unafraid of danger, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Significant reason for eating on the floor?

definitions.text: reason for eating on the floor

blocks.note: first meaning: worth noticing, important

blocks.clueFragment: reason for eating on the floor
blocks.note: second meaning, split in two words: lacking any furniture to eat at

explanation.surface: Asking what important reason people have for eating on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO TABLE, the answer is the playful reason one might eat sitting on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable means remarkable and worth attention, so important; read as two words it explains a floor picnic.

clue.text: Support a method offering retreat

blocks.note: to back is to support
taken as written
a way is a method

explanation.surface: Backing a plan that lets someone withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' could be a noun for a quiet getaway, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To back away is to move backwards or withdraw from a position, which is what retreating means.

clue.text: Young swimmer organising top deal

indicators.note: organising means putting things in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A junior swimming champion negotiating the best contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young swimmer' suggests a sporty child, but it is a young frog.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the larval stage of a frog or toad, living and swimming in water.

clue.text: Attempt to erase discord produced by awful cheater and liar

indicators.note: something awful is in a terrible state, so the letters are in a bad mess

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trying to settle a quarrel caused by a dreadful cheat and a liar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' merely joins the two words of fodder into one set of eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear the air is an idiom for talking openly to resolve tension or a disagreement.

clue.text: Greeted in hospital – wasn’t well

blocks.note: H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital
to ail is to be unwell

explanation.surface: Someone welcomed on a hospital ward because they were sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but nothing goes inside anything; the hospital letter simply comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail someone is to call out or greet them, so hailed is the past tense match.

clue.text: Note lord being heartless – or unthreatening?

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle is removed and only the ends kept

blocks.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
only the outside letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: Asking whether a cruel nobleman is actually harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' suggests a cruel lord, but it removes the inner letters OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Mild means gentle and not harsh or severe, so posing no danger or menace.

clue.text: Looking up, see heights

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading upward runs from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: to spot is to see

explanation.surface: Gazing upward to view the peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking up' fits the surface of peering at summits, but it is the instruction to flip the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tops are the highest points, such as mountain summits, so the plural means peaks or high points.

clue.text: I will join party subsequently as one impressed by false image?

blocks.note: taken as written
a do is a party
later means subsequently

explanation.surface: Someone announcing they will join a political party later, taken in by a false image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics, but it is a social do.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols, statues or images treated as gods, which scripture calls false.

clue.text: Manly six facing trouble

blocks.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
to rile is to annoy or trouble

explanation.surface: Six tough men confronting a difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' looks like a noun being faced, but it is the verb RILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Virile means having strength and masculine energy, a synonym of masculine or manly.

clue.text: Report coming from Oxford is patchy

indicators.note: what comes from within some words is drawn out of their letters

blocks.note: the letters run across these three words

explanation.surface: News from Oxford is inconsistent in quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer starts with the last letter of Oxford and ends inside 'patchy'; 'is' serves in both the surface and the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispatch is an official report or a news story sent by a correspondent.

clue.text: Number, any number, is required for game

blocks.note: ten is a number
n stands for an unspecified number in maths
taken as written

explanation.surface: A game needs a certain number of players, whatever it is.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra, n is the letter for any number at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport played over a net, so one example of a game.
